narrative.overview: The site is a night watch over a small castle workshop: deep indigo, lantern gold and parchment, the palette the Pixel Keep theme already uses. The real work is the hero: product renders sit in pixel frames, and the Xeneon Edge in the hero is drawn as a device, not a screenshot on a card. Everything around the work stays quiet so the work reads first. Game flavour comes from colour, the notched pixel frame and pixel art in the imagery. Text never uses a pixel font: pixel type is hard to read. Night is the default; a sandstone day palette follows the system or the toggle.
keyCharacteristics: Indigo night ground with gold as the single accent.
Notched pixel frames around media, buttons and badges; no rounded cards.
Readable display type (Chakra Petch) over a highly legible body face.
Shelves of projects separated by space and a 4px rule, not by boxes.

rules.name: The One Lantern Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only accent. Teal marks "Free" and nothing else.

rules.name: The Warm Day Rule
rules.body: On sandstone, secondary text is umber; gray text on a coloured ground is refused.

rules.name: The Readable Type Rule
rules.body: No pixel fonts for text, headings included. Pixel art lives in images only.

rules.name: The Title First Rule
rules.body: A project's name comes first; its kind and status sit under it, never above as an eyebrow.

rules.name: The Only Object Rule
rules.body: Only the hardware drawing casts a shadow.

dos: Do put every project's real render or screenshot in a pixel frame before any description.
Do keep store and donation buttons in the Off state until the page exists.
Do check both night and day palettes for 4.5:1 text contrast.
donts: Don't use pixel fonts for any text.
Don't put a label above a heading.
Don't add a second accent colour or gray secondary text on sandstone.
Don't wrap projects in rounded, shadowed cards.
